Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Rearrange Tape Measure
Content: Objective Rearrange tape measure according to avatar size. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Fit to Avatar Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Fit to Avatar Click on the Fit to Avatar icon. Tape measures are now being rearranged automatically to the avatar's size.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with a seamless way to automatically adjust tape measures to match their avatar's size through the Avatar Editor.

Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Show/Hide Individual Tape Measure
Content: Objective Show or hide tape measure individually. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Bottom of the Avatar Editor Window Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Bottom of the Avatar Editor Window Click the check-box to turn it On or Off.
ContentDescription: This web page provides users with the option to individually toggle the visibility of the tape measure in the Avatar Editor through a simple check-box in the main menu.

Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Change Tape Measure Type
Content: Objective Change tape measure type to 'Basic' or 'Surface' as needed. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Bottom of the Avatar Editor Window Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Bottom of the Avatar Editor Window The type of tape measure is now being changed as chosen.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance for changing the tape measure type to 'Basic' or 'Surface' in the Avatar Editor's Main Menu.

Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Open/Save Tape Measure
Content: Objective Save a created tape measure in .mea file format. Open a saved tape measure to reuse it. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Open /Save Operation Open Measurement Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Open Open File window appears. Select a desired file and click Open. Save Measurement Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Save Save File window appears. Select a desired location to store. Enter a desired file name and click Save. .mea file is now being created.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with the functionality to save and open tape measure files in .mea format within the Avatar Editor.

Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Show/Hide All Tape Measure
Content: Objective Show or hide all of the tape measures in the window. Location Main Menu Display Avatar Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window Avatar Display (Mouse-over) Show Avatar Measurements Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Avatar Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window Avatar Display (Mouse-over) Show Avatar Measurements All Avatar tape measures are now being displayed or hidden.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to enable users to easily show or hide all tape measures associated with their avatar in the 3D window for enhanced measurement visibility.

Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Delete Tape Measure
Content: Objective Delete tape measures that are no longer in need. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Delete Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Delete Select a tape measure to delete. Click on the Delete icon. The selected tape measure is now being deleted.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a simple interface for users to efficiently delete unnecessary tape measures from their collection.

Title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Basic/Surface Tape Measurement
Content: Objective Take avatar's measurements such as arm length, back length from projected points. Basic Tape Measurement measures following by its surface curves. Location Main Menu Avatar Measurement Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Measurement Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Click on a point to begin the length measurement. Temporary line appears in purple. Click on any points that need to be included in the process, and double click to end the measurement.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for accurately measuring an avatar's dimensions using basic and surface tape measurement techniques within a 3D environment.

Title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Basic/Surface Circumference Measurement
Content: Objective Take avatar's circumference measurements by measuring its surface curves. There are two options for circumference measurement. Basic Circumference measurement simply measures its circumference. Surface Measurement measures exactly following avatar's shape. Location Main Menu Avatar Measurements Basic Circumference Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Basic/Surface Circumference Measurement Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Measurements Basic Circumference Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Basic/Surface Circumference Measurement Click on one end of desired circumference measurement. Click on the other end. Mouse over a spot between the two points to set the circumference measurement angle. Temporary line appears in purple. Click when the desired angle of the circumference line appears.
ContentDescription: This web page provides detailed instructions for accurately measuring an avatar's circumference using both basic and surface measurement techniques.

Title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Height Measurement
Content: Objective Take avatar's height measurements from the ground to the relevant points. Location Main Menu Avatar Measurement Height Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Height Measurement Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Measurement Height Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Height Measurement Click a point to take the height measurement. Double-click another point to end the height measurement. A light-green colored rectangle indicating the ground automatically appears, and a green line connecting the ground and the clicked point appears to indicate the height.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a detailed guide on how to accurately measure the height of an avatar by utilizing the measurement tools within the 3D interface.

Title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Edit Measurement
Content: Objective Edit avatar measurements. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Tab Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Tab The list of avatar measurements created on the active Avatar appears. Click on the measurement to see or edit its properties. Name Rename the measurement. Basic Length Check the measurement's basic length. Measurement Type Change the measurement type. Surface Length Check the surface length of the measurement. Measurement Information Check the measurement's information. Show Show or hide the selected measurement.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with a comprehensive tool for viewing and editing their avatar's measurements within the Avatar Editor.

Title: Edit 3D Garment Measure
Content: Objective Edit 3D Garment Measure. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Measurement Edit Garment Measure 3D Toolbar Edit Garment Measure Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Measurement Edit Garment Measure 3D Toolbar Edit Garment Measure Click on a 3D Garment Measure to edit. The selected 3D Garment Measure is now being highlighted. Its properties are now being appeared in the Property Editor. Modify the properties of 3D Garment Measure. Linear Garment Measure Circumference Garment Measure Name Rename the Linear Garment Measure. Name Rename the Circumference Garment Measure. Length Confirm the length of the Linear Garment Measure. Surface Length Confirm the length of the Circumference Garment Measure. Square Width Modify the width of the square that appears at the end of the Linear Garment Measure. Circle Diameter Modify the circle diameter that appears with the Circumference Garment Measure.
ContentDescription: This web page provides tools for editing and customizing 3D garment measurements, allowing users to modify properties such as length, width, and diameter through an intuitive interface.

Title: Create 3D Garment Measure
Content: Objective Measure 3D Garment height and circumference. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Measurement Linear/Circumference Garment Measure 3D Toolbar Linear Garment Measure / Circumference Garment Measure Operation Linear Garment Measure Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Measurement Linear Garment Measure 3D Toolbar Linear Garment Measure Click the beginning point of the Linear Garment Measure on a 3D Garment once. A green dot and rectangle appear. While pressing Shift on the keyboard, click the endpoint of the measurement. A vertical measurement with its length is now being created and displayed. Circumference Garment Measure Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Measurement Circumference Garment Measure 3D Toolbar Circumference Garment Measure Click on an area to measure its circumference. A circumference measurement with its value is now being created and displayed.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides clear instructions for accurately measuring the height and circumference of 3D garments using the Linear and Circumference Garment Measure tools.

Title: 3D Snapshot
Content: Objective Save 3D window snapshots from one angle in image file format. Location Main Menu File Snapshot 3D Window (F10) Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Snapshot 3D Window (F10) Save File pop-up window appears. 2. Enter desired file name and location, then click Save. Snapshot window appears. 3. Set details as needed: Single View Image Size Preset Customize or select from provided preset options. Orientation Select from portrait or landscape orientation options. Width Set the width of the image. Height Set the height of the image. Unit Sets the unit of measurement for the image. Resolution Sets the pixels per inch for the image. From ver3.2.0, the image resolution (ppi) will automatically adjust depending on the selected paper size for optimal printing results. Option Transparent Background Save the image with transparent background. Save HTML File A HTML file of the snapshot is also saved. (ver MD10) Reset Resets the options back to the program default settings. Note: Garment Measurements can now be captured in 3D snapshots (ver4.1.0). In order to include Garment Measurements, toggle on the Show Garment Measurements icon in the 3D window.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for saving 3D window snapshots with customizable settings, ensuring users can efficiently capture and store high-quality images for optimal use.

Title: Project with Meta Data (*.ZPrj)/ Garment with Meta Data (*.zpac)
Content: Objective When saving Project files, an accompanying XML file with Garment, trim, and texture information will be provided. Turntable images will also be generated with the Project file (versions after 3.1.38) XML File Contents 1. Product version 2. Garment version 3. Garment polygon, triangle, vertex count: this includes the pattern, trims, textures all information related to the Garment. 3-1. Pattern polygon, triangle, vertex count 3-2. Trim Object polygon, triangle, vertex count: Trim are Object files imported via File Import Import as Trim. 3-3. Button polygon, triangle, and vertex count 3-4. Print Texture polygon, triangle, vertex count: Print Texture are textures imported as Graphic. 3-5. Texture Count: the number of textures applied to Fabric. 3-6. Material Count: the number of items used or applied to Fabric. 4. Avatar total polygon, triangle, and vertex count 5. Turntable image names Location Save as Project: Main Menu Save As Project with Metadata/ Garment with Meta Data Operation Save as Project Navigate to the menu listed in Location. Save File window will appear. Navigate to the desired file location. Enter a file name in File Name, then click the Save button. The Save Metadata dialogue will appear. File Save Folder Saves the Project file along with the metadata and turntable images within a folder. Save .zip File Saves the Project file along with the metadata and turntable images as a ZIP file. Image Image Count Select the number of images for the Turntable. * Don't Show Again Check Box Checking this box will hide the dialog, but will remember the last entered settings when saving the metadata. To view the dialog again, go to Main Menu User Settings Others Metadata, then set the Don't Show Again Save Metadata option to Off.
ContentDescription: This web page provides detailed instructions for saving Project files, including the generation of accompanying XML metadata and turntable images, to ensure comprehensive documentation of garment, trim, and texture information.

Title: 3D Garment Information (ver4.1.0 and Above)
Content: Objective Write and check important Garment information. Location Main Menu File Information Garment Operation Enter Default Garment Information Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Information Garment The Garment Information window appears. Click the Edit icon on the right top corner of the window. The Garment Information window changed to the edit mode. Type in necessary information next to each category and click OK. Typed in information is saved. Add Category Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. Click the Add icon. A category is added. Click the drop-down menu and select desired category. There are eight categories to choose from: Code, Name, Description, Price, Fabric, Size, Colorway, Category, and Memo. Type in necessary information for each category and click OK. Typed in information is saved. Reorder Category Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. Click and drag the category to the desired position. The category is moved to where the mouse is released. When categories are re-ordered completely, click OK. Revised category order is saved. Delete Category Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. Click the Delete icon next to each category. The selected category is deleted. When the editing is completed, click OK. The deleted category no longer appears in the Garment Information window. Note: Toggle on Display When Garment File Loads option to open the Garment Information window every time the file opens. Open or save Garment information such as categories, order, and contents by using the Open and Save buttons on the right top corner of the edit mode. Use the Default File setting to designate default Garment Information file.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide for writing, editing, and managing essential garment information, ensuring users can efficiently enter, reorder, and delete garment categories while saving their changes.

Title: Save User Setting as Configuration File
Content: Objective Save user settings such as language, measurement units, and shortcuts as a configuration file that can be applied to program updates. Location Save Main Menu File Save As User Setting Open Main Menu File Open User Setting Operation Save Configure the user settings as needed. Locate the menu as below : Main Menu File Save As User Setting The Save File window appears. Assign the file name and location, then click Save. The user settings is saved as a configuration file. Open Locate the menu as below : Main Menu File Open User Setting The Open File window appears. Select the desired configuration file and hit the Open button. The information window appears, asking you to restart the program to apply the changes. Restart the program. The user settings contained within the configuration file is applied.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for saving and loading user settings as configuration files to personalize program updates, ensuring a seamless user experience.

Title: Trim (*.trm) Open/Save
Content: Objective Save OBJ files as Trim files. Trim files can be previewed in the Marvelous Designer Library and can be glued to the Garment. Location Save Main Menu File Save As Trim Open Main Menu File Open Trim Operation Save Load an OBJ file as Trim. Follow the indicated guideline below : Main Menu File Save As Trim When there are multiple OBJs in the 3D window, tje Save Trim window appears allowing you to choose the desired OBJ. The Save File window appears. Locate the saving path and file name. Then, click the Save button. The OBJ file is saved Trim file. Open Follow the indicated guideline below : Main Menu File Open Trim The Open File window appears. Select the file to be opened and click Open. The Open Trim window appears. Use the drop-down menu next to Position option to locate the Trim. Original: trim is loaded at its original position when it was saved as a Trim file. Reset: trim is loaded at the center of the 3D window. Note: Hover the mouse over the Trim file in the Library window to preview trim. Click and drag or double lick the Trim file to open from the Library window.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on saving OBJ files as Trim files and managing them within the Marvelous Designer Library for enhanced garment design.

Title: Project File (*.ZPrj) Open/Save
Content: Objective Compress the various files used for Garment creation into one file, and save it. Note: Files included in Project (*.zprj) files *.avt file, with all Avatar-related data [Avatar, Accessories, Arrangement Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points, Avatar Size, Poses] If there are multiple Avatars, they are all saved within the Project file (ver2.3.0). *.zpac file, containing all Garment-related data (3D Garments, 2D Patterns, Fabrics, subsidiary Materials) *.anm file, if an Animation has been recorded Any 3D environment settings (Wind, Light, Ground, Background Image/Color, Scenes/Props) Simulation options set by the user (ver2.3.0). Location Open Project File Main Menu File Open Project (Ctrl+O) Save/Save Over Main Menu File Save Project (Ctrl+S) Save As Main Menu File Save As Project (Ctrl+Shift+S) New Project (ver. 12.1) Main Menu File New Project (Ctrl+N) Operation Open Project File Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Open Project (Ctrl+O) The Open File window opens. Select the desired file and click OK to load the file. Note: Double-click the Project file *.zprj or drag and drop it onto the 3D window to open it. Save Over Project File Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Save Project (Ctrl+S) The original Project file is overwritten. Save Project File Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Save As Project (Ctrl+Shift+S) The Open File window opens. Select a location to save the Garment file. Enter the Project name into the File Name tab and press Save to save the file. A Project file *.zprj will be created along with its thumbnail image. New Project (ver. 12.1) Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File New Project (Ctrl+N) The existing file will be closed and a new Untitled project file will be created.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for compressing and saving garment creation files into a single project file, ensuring all avatar, garment, animation, and environment settings are efficiently organized and accessible.

Title: Motion (*.mtn) Open/Save
Content: Objective Motion is a native file format (*mtn) of Marvelous Designer that saves Avatar movement information, and is used when recording Animation of Garments and Avatars. Marvelous Designer provides Motion files for its default male and female Avatars, but Animation Data or Motion capture Data from third-party 3D solutions can be imported as COLLADA files, then extracted as a Motion file (*mtn) through this menu. Location Open Motion Main Menu File Open Joint Motion Save Motion Main Menu File Save As Joint Motion Operation Open Motion Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Open Joint Motion The Open File window appears. Navigate to the desired *mtn file, then click Open. The Load Motion Type window appears. Select from the available settings: Joint Information Joint Rotation &amp Translation Applies the Avatar's Height, Pose, Motion Data (Joint rotation,) and Joint positions Joint Rotation Only Applies the Pose Motion Data (Joint rotation) only, while maintaining the Avatar's Size. Garment Position Move Avatar &amp Garment to Start Position Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver 2.5.0). Transition Animation A transition Animation is an Animation that changes from a T-Pose to a motion's first Pose in stages, and is created when the Avatar's current Pose and Motion differs from that of the first frame Pose. The motion (*mtn) file loads according to the settings. Save Motion Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Save As Joint Motion The Save File window appears. Type in file name and designate the path the file will be saved to. The Motion (*mtn) file will be saved to the designated path. Note: Motion files can only be saved when imported as Avatars in COLLADA format with Motion Data, and the COLLADA files must be in Open COLLADA format. To learn more about COLLADA format, please reference 3D File (COLLADA) Import. The Transition Animation for default avatars of version10 is not compatible with the previous versions.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on managing Objective Motion (*mtn) files in Marvelous Designer, detailing how to import, save, and utilize Avatar movement data for garment animation.

Title: Pose (*.pos) Open/Save
Content: Objective Use this function to load an Avatars Pose or location information. If a Pose file is loaded the Simulation button is automatically turned on and the Avatar gradually changes from the current Pose to the new Pose. The Garments worn by the Avatar are also simulated. Location Open Pose (Change) Main Menu File Open Pose (Ctrl+Shift+P) Save Pose Main Menu File Save As Pose Operation Open Pose (Change) Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Open Pose (Ctrl+Shift+P) The Simulation automatically turns on and the Avatar's Pose changes. While the Pose is being changed, the Play Motion tool or Simulation tool can be clicked to stop the Pose. Click Play Motion tool or Simulation tool to restart the pose change. Save Pose Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Save As Pose The Save File window appears. Type in the file name and designate the path the file is saved to. Select Save. The Pose (*.pos) file is saved. Open/Load Hand Pose (ver.2024.1) Load an avatar into the scene. Load hand pose file (.hpos) or Pose file (.pos) In the Open Pose dialog box select the type of Joint Information Partial Pose (Both Hands, Left Hand, or Right Hand). Click OK button. The pose is applied to selected hands only. Note: The (.hpos) file is a format that deals only with the hand pose. The hand pose can be applied among all poses through the .pos file. The (.hpos) is provided as downloadable content in the Library (ver.2024.1). The library (.hpos) files only apply to Female_V2 and Male_V2 avatar types. Load Pose Type When importing a Pose with joints differing from the original Avatar, the Pose type can be set like below: Avatar Size + Joint Rotation &amp Position (Ver. 10) Applies the Avatar's Size, Pose, Motion Data (joint rotation) and Joint positions. Joint Rotation Only (Ver. 10) Applies the Pose Motion Data (Joint rotation) only, while maintaining the Avatar's Size. Cancel or re-load Avatars using the Ctrl + Z, Ctrl + Y keys (ver5.0.0.) Open Pose Dialogue Box (ver. 2024.1) Pose Only (Maintain Avatar Size) Applies the Avatar's Size, Pose, Motion Data (joint rotation) and Joint positions. Pose &amp Joint Translation Applies the Pose Motion Data (Joint rotation) only, while maintaining the Avatar's Size. Partial Pose Full Body Apply Pose file to full body. Both Hands Apply Partial Pose file to both hands. Left hand Apply Partial Pose file to left hand only. Right hand Apply Partial Pose file to right hand only. Maintain Current Shoe Pose Maintains shoe pose while applying additional pose information. Align Bottom to ground Align bottom of avatar to ground after applying pose information. Reset While the dialog box is running, reset settings to default Apply Apply pose based on the input values entered. Cancel Close the dialog box without applying Note: If a Pose file is loaded, the simulation is automatically turned on and the avatar changes from the current Pose to the new Pose. End Result Avatar's pose (.pos) file and hand pose (.hpos) file is applied, and avatar change to the applied pose.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides functionality for loading and saving avatar poses and locations, allowing users to seamlessly transition between poses while simulating garment dynamics.

Title: 3D Garment (*.zpac) Open/Add/Save
Content: Objective Save the 3D Garment and 2D Pattern contents together in a *.zpac file format. Save the Garment to the users computer, or open and edit a saved Garment file. Location Open Garment Main Menu File Open Garment Add Garment Main Menu File Add Garment Save Garment Main Menu File Save As Garment New Garment (ver. 12.1) Main Menu File New Garment (Ctrl+Shift+N) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Select the desired file and click Open to load it. Note: Garment files (*.zpac) and Project files (*.zprj) can be opened by double clicking them or dragging and dropping them onto the 3D window. Open Auto Save File If the program is closed abnormally while a Garment is being worked on, a pop-up window saying Autosave file exists, do you want to recover the autosave file? appears when the program runs again. Click Yes to load the autosave file or click No to refrain from loading the autosave file. (Project File (*.zprj) is auto saved from ver3.1.0.) Add Garment Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Add Garment Select a Garment file and click Open. The Add Garment window appears (ver2.4.0) Select the appropriate settings and click OK to place the Garment Note: * A Garment can be added by right clicking on the Library's Garment file and using the Add to Workplace menu. * Add Garment Settings Placement X Placement long the X axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. Y Placement long the Y axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. Z Placement long the Z axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. Unit Unit for placement. New Garment (ver. 12.1) Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File New Garment (Ctrl+Shift+N) All existing cloth will be removed and a new "Untitled" project file will be created.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for saving, opening, and managing 3D garment and 2D pattern files in the *.zpac format, ensuring users can efficiently create and edit their garment designs.

Title: Marvelous Designer File Format
Content: Marvelous Designer File Format Type Format Description Garment *.zpac Contains information on Garments, Patterns, Sewing, and Fabrics. Project *.zprj Compresses the various files used for Garment creation into one file, and saves it. The Project file contains the AVT file that has Avatar-related data [Avatar, Accessories, Arrangement Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points, Avatar size, Poses] and the ZPac file that contains Garment-related data [3D Garments, 2D Patterns, Fabrics, subsidiary Material], as well as an animation file if there is animation. Avatar *.avt Contains all the information related to Avatars (Model, Sizing data, Poses, Motions, Accessories, Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points). Pose *.pos Avatar Pose information that, automatically saved whenever the Garment is saved. The Avatars Pose can easily be changed with this file. Avatar Poses from other software can only be saved when the Avatar is a COLLADA file with joints. Joint Motion *.mtn Contains Avatar Motion information. As with the Pose file, can only be saved on COLLADA file Avatars with joint and Animation information. Fabric *.zfab Contains the property values (texture + physical properties) of the set Fabric. Physical Property *.psp Contains the detailed values of Fabric Physical Properties. Topstitch *.sst Contains the type, number of lines, thread thickness, SPI, length, etc. Button *.btn Contains the type, size, and color of Buttons. Buttonhole *.bth Contains the tyle, size, and color of the Buttonholes. Arrangement Point *.arr Arrangement Points are the blue points that are distributed around the Avatar, and are used to arrange Patterns easily around the Avatar. Arrangement Points are created on top of the Arrangement Bounding Volume covering the surroundings of the Avatar. Arrangement Bounding Volume *.pan Arrangement Bounding Volumes are the green cylinders covering each part of the Avatar, and each end of a cylinder is connected to an Avatars joint. As such, even if the Avatars Pose is changed, the cylinder simply adjusts to the changed Pose and can be used as it is. Tape Measure *.mea It has the information of the tape measure created in the avatar. Camera Projection *.cmp Contains the camera's Field of View information (near, far, etc.). Camera Transformation *.cmt Contains camera view information of the 3D Garment window. Simulation Property *.smp Contains settings for Simulation.
ContentDescription: Explore the comprehensive file formats used in Marvelous Designer for garment creation, including detailed descriptions of garment, avatar, pose, fabric, and simulation properties.

Title: 3D Garment Surface Textures - Save
Content: Objective Save all texture images used on Garments and subsidiary Materials to a designated folder. Surface textures can also be cropped to a desired size before they are saved (ver2.5.0). Location Main Menu File Save As Surface Textures Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Save As Surface Textures The Save File window appears. Select a Folder location to save the Surface Textures, then press Save. The Save Surface Textures window appears. Select from the available settings. Original Size Saves the surface textures in its original size. Crop Fabric Textures Crops the image file based on the value entered. Click OK. The selected image size setting is applied and the files are saved to the Folder location assigned. Note: Surface textures refers to the surface texture of a Garment.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for saving and cropping surface texture images of garments and related materials to a designated folder.

Title: Project File (*.Zprj) Add
Content: Objective Add Garments and Avatars contained within Project files to the workspace (ver2.3.0). Location Main Menu File Add Project Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Add Project Navigate and select the Project file to be added and click Open. The Add Project window appears. Apply any detailed settings, then click on the OK button. Note: Add Project Options Object Garment (.zpac) Checking the box will add the Garment compressed in the Project file. Avatar (.avt) Checking the box will add the Avatar compresses in the Project file. Translation X Move added items horizontally along the center of the 3D environment. Y Move added items vertically along the center of the 3D environment. Z Move added items front and back along the center of the 3D environment. Unit Select the measurement unit for translation. Right click on Project files directly in the Library window and select Add to Workspace from the pop-up menu to add Garments and/or Avatars contained within Project files.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adding Garments and Avatars from Project files to your workspace in version 2.3.0, ensuring a seamless integration of assets into your 3D environment.

Title: Avatar (*.avt) Open/Save
Content: Objective Save and load all Avatar related files, such as the Model (*.dae or *obj), Pose (*.pos), Motion (*.mtn), Accessories (*.acc), Bounding Volume (*.pan), and Arrangement Points (*.arr) as one file (*.avt). Location Open AVT Main Menu File Open Avatar (Ctrl+Shift+A) Save AVT Main menu File Save As Avatar Operation Open AVT Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Open Avatar (Ctrl+Shift+A) The Open File window appears. Select the desired file and click Open to load it. Note: The default avatars provided by Marvelous Designer are located in the following path. Windows Library Documents Marvelous Designer Assets_ver_x.x.x Avatar Avatar (Detail Path) C: Users User Name Documents Marvelous Designer Assets_ver_x.x.x Avatar Avatar Save AVT Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Save As Avatar The Open File window appears. Select a location to save the Garment file, enter in a name and press Save button. Note: Even if multiple Avatars exist within the workspace, they can be saved separately (ver2.3.0).
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidelines for saving and loading all Avatar-related files in Marvelous Designer, allowing users to manage their Avatar assets efficiently.

Title: 3D Garment (*.zpac) Add
Content: Objective Add an extra Garment to the current Garment to coordinate. Location Main Menu File Add Garment Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Add Garment Select a Garment file and click Open. The Add Garment window appears (ver2.4.0.) Select the appropriate settings and click OK to place the Garment Note: A Garment can be added by right clicking on the Library's Garment file and using the Add to Workplace menu. Add Garment Settings Placement X Placement long the X axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. Y Placement long the Y axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. Z Placement long the Z axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. Unit Unit for placement.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for adding and positioning an extra garment within the 3D workspace, ensuring seamless coordination with existing garments.

Title: Avatar (*.avt) Add
Content: Objective Use the Add Avatar function to load and work on several Avatars from the 3D Garment window in one go. This function can be used when loading and coordinating belt buckles, buttons, armor, and other hard objects. Furthermore, it can also be used when designing Garments that are connected to two avatars. Location Main Menu File Add Avatar Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Add Avatar The Open File window appears. Select the Avatar to be added and click Open. The Add Avatar window appears (ver2.4.0). Select the appropriate settings and click OK to place the Avatar. Note: Add Avatar Options Placement X Move along the X axis (left, right) relative to the center of the 3D Window. Y Move along the Y axis (top, bottom) relative to the center of the 3D Window. Z Move along the Z axis (front, back) relative to the center of the 3D Window. Unit Set unit for placement. As shown in the image below, the Add Avatar function can load and use human-shaped Avatars, as well as parts needed for production, such as helmets, shoulder pads, armor and petticoats. When using multiple Avatars, save as Project file to save all Avatars (ver2.3.0).
ContentDescription: The "Add Avatar" function allows users to efficiently load and coordinate multiple 3D Avatars and their accessories for garment design, enhancing creativity and productivity in the design process.

Title: Open Auto Save File (.Zpac or .Zprj)
Content: Objective Open files that are auto-saved when the program closes unexpectedly due to a power failure or error. Note: From ver3.1.0, project file (*.zprj) will be auto saved. File is auto saved every three minutes. Therefore, auto save files only contains work completed three minutes prior to power/ program failure. Location By Opening the Program Launch Marvelous Designer Auto Save File pop-up By Locating the File C: Users User Name Documents Marvelous Designer Assets_ver_x.x.x Autosave Operation By Opening the Program Follow the indicated guideline below: Launch Marvelous Designer Auto Save File pop-up The auto-saved file opens. By Opening the Folder Follow the indicated guideline below: C: Users User Name Documents Marvelous Designer Assets_ver_x.x.x Autosave Double-click autosave.zpac/ autosave.zprj file created in the folder. The program starts and the auto saved file opens. Note: Auto Save File Location You can changed the folder in which Auto Save files are saved via (ver2.3.0): Main Menu Settings User Settings Default Files Auto Save Select file path
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on how to access and restore auto-saved files in Marvelous Designer after unexpected program closures or power failures.

Title: Show / Hide 3D Color (Ver. 2024.1)
Content: Objective Toggle on and off the color of the state (Freeze, Solidify, Strengthen, Layer, Subdivide) applied to Pattern and Mesh in the 3D Window. Location 3D Background Options Menu Show/Hide Color Operation Using 3D Background Options Menu Right-click the background in 3D window to activate menu Select Show/Hide color Select preferred option Note: This can be executed for Pattern and Mesh, respectively. Not only can you show/hide individually, but you can also show/hide them all. End Result State defined color (freeze, solidify, strengthen, layer, subdivide) should now be hidden when menu options are selected.
ContentDescription: This web page provides users with instructions on how to toggle the visibility of state-defined colors (Freeze, Solidify, Strengthen, Layer, Subdivide) for Patterns and Meshes in the 3D Window via the 3D Background Options Menu

Title: Wind Controller Setting (Above ver. 2024.0)
Content: Objective You can add a wind effect to the 3D Window to create the impression that your garment is being affected by the wind. You can change the wind settings with several options. Location Main Menu Display Environment Show Wind Controller View icon in 3D Window Environment Show Wind Controller Operation Activate Wind Effect 1. Follow this path The wind controller appears in a 3D window in the shape of a wind. 2. Click the Wind controller A gizmo appears on the Wind controller and properties for the wind appear in the Property Editor. 3. click the checkbox under Wind Activate. The Activate checkbox will be ticked to activate the wind. 4. Click the Simulation button. Wind is activated in the 3D window. Wind Direction Setting 1. Follow this path Main menu View Environment view icon Show Wind Controller The wind controller appears in a 3D window in the shape of a wind. 2. Click on the Wind Controller The gizmo is activated. 3. Use the gizmo to adjust the position and direction of the wind, the wind flows in the direction of the icon and arrow. 4. Click Simulation. In the 3D window, the wind blows at the position and direction you adjusted. Multiple Wind Setting 1. Create or duplicate a Wind Controller. Create: Scene Browser Select Wind group, Right-click Create Wind Duplicate: Scene Browser Select Wind Controller in the Wind group, Right-click Duplicate Environment icon in 3D Window window View Wind Controller Select Wind icon in 3D window Right-click Duplicate Wind Properties Setting 1. Follow the corresponding path: Main Menu View Show Wind Controller The Wind Controller appears in the 3D Window. 2. Click the wind controller. The properties for the wind appear in the Property Editor. 3. In the Property Editor, set the wind options according to your preference. Name Changes name of the wind according to the user preference. Wind Activate Sets the activation status of the wind. Unlimited Bound It is activated by default and affects the whole space depending on its position and direction. Type Type Sets the type of the wind. Spherical: The wind blows in spherical shape, in every direction starting from the Wind Controller. Planar: The wind blows only from the designated direction, regardless of the Wind Controller's location. Strength Sets the intensity of the wind. The higher the value, the stronger the wind. Decay [0~100] Sets the range of the wind. The wind draws an arc and blows weaker according to the set value of wind intensity. If the value is "0", it blows in a straight line endlessly. Frequency (sec) Sets the cycle of the wind. The wind repeatably blows weaker and stronger in interval of set value of seconds. If the value is "0", it blows regularly. Turbulence [0~100] Sets the turbulence of wind intensity. The higher the value, the more irregular the wind intensity. Rotation Key Activate Activate to allow the wind animation rotation value to be set by the animation key. Translation X Sets Key to the X position value Y Sets Key to the Y position value Z Sets Key to the Z position value
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to add and customize wind effects in a 3D environment, enhancing the realism of garment simulations.
